note: Reference ONLY: the studio shell is free and MIT, but using it means paying the MuAPI gateway per generation (paid dependency - barred by the FREE-only rule), and the free local engines need a GPU the fleet does not have. Nothing in VyralX calls this studio's generation path; MultiModelStudio.generate() refuses honestly. What VyralX keeps is the multi-studio LAYOUT pattern below, for a future creation console.
pattern: One studio per modality (image, video, lip sync, cinema) plus a workflow studio that chains them; a shared prompt/model picker and an upload-history picker sit across all studios.

studios.name: Image Studio
studios.purpose: Text-to-image and image-to-image generation across many models, with multi-image input.
studios.vyralx_note: Pattern for a future thumbnail/poster studio: one prompt, model picker, reference images.

studios.name: Video Studio
studios.purpose: Text-to-video and image-to-video generation across many models.
studios.vyralx_note: Pattern for a future clip studio: same prompt/model picker shape as Image Studio, video outputs.

studios.name: Lip Sync Studio
studios.purpose: Animate portraits or sync lips to audio (image-based and video-based models).
studios.vyralx_note: Pattern for a future talking-head/avatar step in the shorts pipeline.

studios.name: Cinema Studio
studios.purpose: Long-form / cinematic generation controls and multi-shot workflows.
studios.vyralx_note: Pattern for a future long-form lane: shot list, consistent style, multi-shot assembly.

studios.name: Workflows Studio
studios.purpose: Chained multi-step generation workflows across studios.
studios.vyralx_note: Pattern closest to VyralX's own pipeline orchestration: stages with explicit inputs/outputs and approval gates.

unverified_note: The upstream README lists 14 studios; only the 5 above are named in the verified registry card. The remaining 9 names are NOT listed here rather than guessed - verify from the upstream README before citing them.
